questions.prompt: Where the bishop had once dwelt, there now a deep silence lies.
questions.answer: Ubi episcopus ōlim habitāverat, ibi nunc altum silentium iacet.

questions.prompt: We do not know whither the fugitives fled through the dark woods.
questions.answer: Quō fugitīvī per silvās obscūrās fūgerint nescīmus.

questions.prompt: The scouts hastened to report whence so great a danger had arisen.
questions.answer: Explōrātōrēs, unde tantum discrīmen ortum esset, nūntiāre properāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Hither the weary soldiers came, whence they never returned.
questions.answer: Hūc mīlitēs fessī vēnērunt, unde numquam rediērunt.

questions.prompt: When the enemy attacked, then the citizens bravely took up arms.
questions.answer: Cum hostēs oppugnāvērunt, tum cīvēs fortiter arma cēpērunt.

questions.prompt: As often as the poet recited, so often the crowd eagerly applauded.
questions.answer: Quotiēns poēta recitābat, totiēns turba cupidē plausit.

questions.prompt: When will the parent return, whom we now so anxiously await?
questions.answer: Quandō pārēns redībit, quem nunc tam sollicitē exspectāmus?

questions.prompt: Then the fields were fertile; now they lie barren and abandoned.
questions.answer: Tunc agrī fēcundī erant; nunc sterilēs et dēsertī iacent.

questions.prompt: So fierce was the battle that few soldiers survived that day.
questions.answer: Tam ātrōx erat proelium ut paucī mīlitēs illum diem superessent.

questions.prompt: The wine, somewhat diluted, was divided among the guests.
questions.answer: Vīnum, aliquantum dīlūtum, inter convīvās dīvīsum est.

questions.prompt: The old man is now as greedy as once he was generous.
questions.answer: Tam avārus nunc est senex quam ōlim līberālis fuit.

questions.prompt: How greatly you fear death, of which you so rarely think!
questions.answer: Quam magnopere mortem timēs, dē quā tam rārō cōgitās!

questions.prompt: Somewhere in these mountains the exiles are hiding, though we scarcely believe it.
questions.answer: Alicubī in hīs montibus exsulēs latent, quamquam vix crēdimus.

questions.prompt: If ever the tyrant returns, the people will flee to some place afar.
questions.answer: Sī umquam tyrannus redierit, populus aliquō procul fugiet.

questions.prompt: From somewhere a rumor arose that the fleet had been destroyed.
questions.answer: Alicunde fāma orta est classem dēlētam esse.

questions.prompt: By this way the merchants used to travel, by that the shepherds drove their flocks.
questions.answer: Hāc mercātōrēs iter facere solēbant, illāc pāstōrēs gregēs agēbant.

questions.prompt: Where the road narrows, there the ambush was cleverly prepared.
questions.answer: Quā via angustātur, ibi īnsidiae callidē parātae sunt.

questions.prompt: Here the temple once stood; there, across the valley, the citadel rose.
questions.answer: Hīc templum ōlim stābat; illīc, trāns vallem, arx surgēbat.

questions.prompt: By some way or other the messenger slipped through the enemy's lines.
questions.answer: Aliquā nūntius per hostium ōrdinēs ēlāpsus est.

questions.prompt: Whither the raft would be carried by the current, no helmsman could foresee.
questions.answer: Quō ratis flūmine ferrētur, nūllus gubernātor praevidēre poterat.

questions.prompt: As often as the Danaans attacked, so often the walls of Troy repelled them.
questions.answer: Quotiēns Danaī oppugnāvērunt, totiēns Trōiae mūrī eōs reppulērunt.

questions.prompt: When the boy first entered the elementary school, then he began to fear the master.
questions.answer: Cum puer prīmum lūdum litterārium intrāvit, tum magistrum timēre coepit.

questions.prompt: Now he demands a bronze cauldron, which somewhere he had lost.
questions.answer: Nunc aēneum lebētem flāgitat, quem alicubī āmīserat.
